bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The company’s institutional sales (railways, e-buses) are not just a side business—they are a margin anchor with long-term visibility tied to government infrastructure spending; the 60% export mix is not commodity-driven but brand-led, with Responsive’s name on retail shelves in the U.S.—a rarity among Indian manufacturers
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Scale leadership: states it is India's largest manufacturer of PVC-based products and ranks 5th largest globally, and is among the top 5 producers of vinyl flooring globally
- Distribution reach: presence in all Indian states through a network of over 100 distributors (the Corporate Overview spread separately states '75+ distributors across India' - the two figures conflict) and more than 300 international distributors across 70 countries
- Installed base / references: more than 5,000 projects completed, and described as 'a vendor of repute' to hospitality, medical and other commercial institutions
- Longevity and single-site integration: established 1982, 40+ years of manufacturing expertise on a single 100-acre integrated manufacturing campus at Boisar
- Breadth of range: 30+ product categories across flooring, synthetic leather, ropes and waterproofing membranes, serving 25+ end-user industries - reduces dependence on any one application
- Developed-market presence: extensive retail presence across Europe and North America, a channel most Indian PVC peers do not claim
- Management systems: ISO 9001 / ISO 14001 / ISO 45001 certified manufacturing unit with designated safety personnel, safety committees and external partners; BRSR limited assurance by an external provider
- Industry context flagged by management (not a company-specific claim): 'Backward integration is becoming a key competitive advantage' - the Company does not state that it is itself backward integrated
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Imported PVC resin dependence and Chinese oversupply - a structural squeeze on the Company's only input and its selling prices — Management states 'margin pressure from imported PVC resin and Chinese competition remains a major concern' even while calling the 2025-2030 market outlook structurally positive, and lists as important industry dynamics that 'India remains heavily dependent on imported PVC resin', 'Chinese oversupply is suppressing prices globally' and 'Domestic players are lobbying for anti-dumping and BIS protections'. It separately warns that 'Volatility in raw material prices due to fluctuation in resin prices may hinder industry expansion over coming years'. This is the sharpest structural risk in the report because the Company is a single-input, single-polymer manufacturer with no disclosed backward integration - management itself notes 'Backward integration is becoming a key competitive advantage' without claiming to have any, so the relief valve it identifies is one it does not hold. Any protection would come from anti-dumping/BIS action the Company does not control.
- Single-segment, single-domestic-plant concentration - no diversification anywhere in the operating structure — The MD&A states 'The Company is engaged only in single segment of products i.e. PVC products'; BRSR Section A item 16 shows one main activity, Manufacturing, at 100% of turnover; and BRSR item 18 records just one national plant (plus two offices), the Boisar facility in Palghar district, Thane, Maharashtra. Every rupee of standalone revenue therefore depends on one polymer, one process family and one physical site - fire, flood, labour action, a Maharashtra pollution-control order or a resin-supply interruption at Boisar has no fallback. A second, international plant appears in the BRSR location table but is never named, located or described anywhere in the report, so it cannot be relied on as redundancy.
- Export concentration colliding with tariffs and war - management explicitly attributes damage to it this year — BRSR item 19(b) puts exports at 30.45% of total turnover, with more than 300 international distributors across 70 countries and an extensive retail presence in Europe and North America - i.e. roughly a third of standalone revenue sits outside India's jurisdiction and currency. Management links this directly to FY26 damage, commenting in the key-ratio disclosure that 'Surged tariffs and escalating war tension impacted the business of the Company' and that 'Geopolitical tensions and war increased global instability and economic stress' (the associated ratio figures are deliberately not reproduced here). This is a stated, realised risk rather than a hypothetical one, and the Company has no disclosed hedging, alternative-market or tariff-mitigation plan.
- Receivables and working-capital stretch tied to the export channel — Management's own commentary on its key financial ratios flags a material lengthening of debtor days, explained by surged tariffs and escalating war tension, and a decline in interest coverage explained by geopolitical tension and war; it also notes the current ratio rose because of an increase in trade receivables coupled with a decrease in short-term borrowings. Read qualitatively, cash is being absorbed into receivables rather than released, and the improvement in one headline liquidity ratio is partly an artefact of that absorption - a durable watch-item for anyone tracking this company. Numeric ratio values are deliberately not reproduced here.
- Sharp workforce contraction and inconsistent headcount disclosure — The MD&A states that as on March 31, 2026 the Company had 273 employees against 358 in the previous year - a reduction of roughly a quarter of the payroll in a single year - while asserting industrial relations at the factory 'have remained cordial' and offering no explanation for the decline. The BRSR reports 275 permanent employees and 102 permanent workers at the same date, which does not reconcile with the MD&A's 273 figure, and reports permanent-employee turnover of 9.02% in FY26 against 8.15% and 2.16% in the two prior years (a rising trend), with the permanent-workers turnover row left entirely blank. For a business whose only manufacturing know-how sits at one site, a shrinking and increasingly mobile workforce with contradictory reporting is a structural, not cosmetic, concern.
- Product safety, quality and VOC/environmental regulation of PVC products — The BRSR material-issues table identifies Product Safety and Quality (classified, oddly, as an Opportunity) and states that 'any loose end in the product maintenance or quality may pose it to material risks', with financial implications spelled out as product recalls, damaged consumer quality perception, reputational harm and increased costs from replacements, field service, product fixes and litigation. The MD&A reinforces the regulatory leg: 'stringent regulations related to volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emissions coupled with changing environmental policies could also affect overall business prospects during forecasted timeframe'. PVC flooring sold into healthcare, education and transportation is exactly the category where VOC and indoor-air-quality rules tighten first, and roughly a third of output goes to jurisdictions (Europe, North America) that regulate this most aggressively. NOTE A CLEAR TEMPLATE DEFECT IN THIS ROW: the mitigation text reads 'Our product responsibility extends beyond manufacturing and sales, contributing to cleaner and safer mobility' - 'mobility' is automotive-sector boilerplate that does not describe a PVC flooring and synthetic-leather business, indicating this material-issue row was copied from another company's BRSR.
- Data privacy and cyber security — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a Risk with negative financial implications: 'technology failures or cyberattacks can disrupt operations, leading to downtime and loss of productivity'. Stated mitigations are firewalls, encryption, multi-factor authentication, regular security audits, employee education and adoption of global data protection standards, plus regular assessment for system vulnerabilities, compliance gaps and technological obsolescence. No incidents, breaches or spend are disclosed, and there is no board-level technology committee.
- Business ethics and code-of-conduct compliance — The first material issue in the BRSR table, classified as a Risk: 'Non-compliance of code of conduct and business ethics affects the work environment and profitability of the Company and may also cause financial or reputational impact', with negative financial implications from disruption and reputational damage. The only stated mitigation is regular employee training on the Code of Conduct. This risk sits alongside a related-party disclosure whose AOC-2 paragraph is self-contradictory (it simultaneously suggests material related-party transactions may exist and that no information need be provided) and a BRSR that reports the entire related-party-share block as dashes.
- Governance and senior-management instability - board and KMP churn plus internally contradictory disclosure — Inside FY26 the independent-director bench turned over almost entirely: Dr. Anita Shantaram resigned 05-11-2025, Ms. Mita Jha ceased 21-12-2025 on her untimely demise, and two new independent directors were appointed (11-11-2025 and 04-02-2026). Both KMP finance/secretarial posts fell vacant - the CFO ceased 12-01-2026 and the Company Secretary on 31-03-2026 - and were only filled after year-end (CFO 13-04-2026, CS 04-05-2026), leaving the CFO chair empty for about three months. After year-end two Non-Executive Non-Independent Directors, Mr. Rishabh Agarwal and Mr. Aayush Agarwal, both ceased on the same date, 26-05-2026. The report is also internally inconsistent about who chairs the board (Corporate Governance Report: Mr. Rishabh Agarwal; Corporate Information and the Corporate Overview: Mr. Aayush Agarwal) and lists a CFO as a KMP 'as of March 31, 2026' whom the same report says ceased on 12-01-2026. Directors attended between 1 and 5 of the 5 board meetings. Documentary self-contradiction of this density is itself an information-quality risk for anyone relying on these filings.

business.body: Established in 1982, the Company manufactures and sells articles made out of PVC/polymers, with product verticals comprising Vinyl Flooring, Synthetic Leather, Luxury Vinyl Tile (LVT) and Stone Plastic Composite (SPC), Synthetic ropes and Waterproof Membrane (PVC specialised covers), spanning 30+ product categories. It sells to residential, commercial, industrial, healthcare, hospitality, transportation, education, sports, IT, telecom, retail and real-estate customers through a domestic distributor network and more than 300 international distributors, having completed over 5,000 projects. The Company reports itself as operating in a single business segment (PVC products); within the BRSR product mix Vinyl Flooring is the largest turnover contributor, followed by Synthetic Leather and Synthetic ropes, while 'PVC Intermediaries' is shown with a dash, i.e. a stated nil contribution.

business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Responsive Industries Limited, Hong Kong ('RIL HK') — subsidiary: Wholly owned - 100% of shares held by the listed entity (BRSR Section A item 23). The Company's ONLY material subsidiary as on March 31, 2026 under the Regulation 16(1)(c) materiality policy (income or net worth exceeding ten percent of consolidated income or net worth). Because it also crosses the twenty-percent Regulation 24(1) threshold, Ms. Jeny Vinod Kumar Gowadia, Independent Director of the Company, was appointed to its board w.e.f. February 13, 2026. Minutes of its board meetings are placed before the Company's Board for review and noting. Does not participate in the listed entity's Business Responsibility initiatives, and the BRSR reporting boundary is standalone only - so the group's largest subsidiary sits entirely outside the sustainability disclosure. Its activity is never described anywhere in the routed text. Financial columns from Form AOC-1 Part A deliberately not extracted.
- Responsive Industries LLC, USA — subsidiary: Wholly owned - 100% of shares held by the listed entity (BRSR Section A item 23); financial year ending March 31, 2026; reporting currency US Dollar. Does not participate in the listed entity's Business Responsibility initiatives. No description of its activity (distribution, manufacturing or marketing arm) is given anywhere in the routed text, although the Company states extensive retail presence across North America. Financial columns from Form AOC-1 Part A deliberately not extracted.
- Axiom Cordages Limited, Hong Kong — subsidiary: Wholly owned - 100% of shares held by the listed entity (BRSR Section A item 23); financial year ending March 31, 2026; reporting currency US Dollar. Does not participate in the listed entity's Business Responsibility initiatives. The AR gives no description of what this entity does; the parent separately reports a 'Synthetic ropes' product vertical in BRSR item 17 but never links the two - any connection is unstated and must not be assumed. Financial columns from Form AOC-1 Part A deliberately not extracted.
- NO associates or joint ventures (stated absence) — associate: Form AOC-1 note 2 states: 'Since the Company does not have any Associates or Joint Venture, information pertaining to Part B to this form relating to Associates and Joint Venture is not given.' Note 1 states that names of subsidiaries liquidated or sold during the year is 'Nil'. BRSR item 23 likewise lists no holding company - the AR discloses no holding or ultimate holding entity above Responsive Industries Limited. DEFECT in Form AOC-1 Part A: row 14 '% of shareholding' is printed with NO values against any of the three subsidiaries - the shareholding percentages used here come instead from BRSR Section A item 23, which states 100% for each.
- Related-party transactions - counterparties NOT disclosed — related party: The Directors' Report states all contracts/arrangements/transactions with related parties during FY ended March 31, 2026 were in the ordinary course of business and on an arm's length basis with no conflict with the Company's interest, were compliant with the Companies Act 2013, SEBI LODR and the Company's RPT Policy, were reviewed and approved by the Audit Committee and the Board, are placed before the Audit Committee quarterly (including omnibus-approved repetitive transactions) and are subject to independent review by the Statutory and Secretarial Auditors. NO counterparty is named and NO Form AOC-2 content is provided. DEFECT - the AOC-2 sentence as printed is self-contradictory and appears to have dropped a negation: 'The Company may have entered into any contract/ arrangement/ transaction with related parties which could be considered material, or which may have potential conflict with the interest of the Company; hence there is no information to be provided as required under section 134(3)(h)...', closing with 'shall be disclosed, if applicable.' Read literally it asserts material related-party transactions may exist AND that nothing need be disclosed. The RPT extract is truncated mid-word ('Statutory and Secretarial Auditors of the Com'). Separately, BRSR Principle 1 Essential Indicator 9 shows the entire 'Share of RPTs in purchases / sales / loans & advances / investments' block as dashes for both years - stated nil rather than blank.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Move down-market into the residential segment: currently supplying vinyl flooring to hospitality, medical facilities and other commercial institutions, the Company states 'aggressive plans to cater to the residential markets first via the B2B route and eventually by going retail' - an explicit two-step channel strategy (B2B first, retail later).
- Pursue a stated '$1 Billion Vision' built on three named planks - Infrastructure, Innovation and the 'Make in India' Advantage - while positioning as a leading manufacturer of SPC, LVT and resilient flooring solutions. No date is attached to the vision anywhere in the routed text.
- Lean on product development and new-product introduction as a growth lever: the outlook explicitly names 'strong product development' and 'market efforts' alongside increased capacity utilisation as the basis for growth optimism, and the industry commentary notes companies are introducing innovative products with better performance features.
- Raise utilisation of the existing single Boisar plant rather than announce new capacity: the only outlook sentence in the MD&A rests on 'increased capacity utilization'. No new plant, line or capex project is mentioned anywhere in this bundle.
- Defend and extend the leadership position - India's largest PVC-products manufacturer with presence in all states via 100+ distributors, 5th largest globally with 300+ international distributors across 70 countries, and extensive retail presence in developed Europe and North America.
- Note on what is NOT stated: although management identifies 'Backward integration is becoming a key competitive advantage' as an important industry dynamic, the Company does not state any intent, plan or project to backward integrate itself. Similarly, domestic players are said to be 'lobbying for anti-dumping and BIS protections' without the Company claiming to lead or join that effort.
- Dividend: the Board has recommended a final dividend of Re. 0.10 per equity share of Re. 1 each (a rate of 10%) for FY 2025-26, stated to be in accordance with the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy which is published at https://www.responsiveindustries.com/policies/. The AGM notice puts this to shareholders as an ordinary resolution declaring the dividend 'and the same be paid out of the profits of the Company', payable to members on the register as on the cut-off date after deduction of tax at source. This is the only distribution mechanism disclosed - no buyback, no bonus, no debt-reduction plan, no credit rating and no reinvestment quantum appears anywhere in this bundle. Reserves: the Board does not propose to transfer any amount to reserves for the year ended March 31, 2026 (back-filled with provenance from the sibling profile.txt bundle, Directors' Report Section 7 - it is not present in the governance routing). Equity base: paid-up equity share capital of Rs. 26,66,08,544 comprising 26,66,08,544 equity shares of Re. 1 each fully paid-up, against authorised capital of Rs. 1,22,00,00,000, so roughly four-fifths of the authorised capital is unissued headroom (paid-up figure corroborated independently in BRSR Section A item 11; authorised capital back-filled from the sibling profile.txt bundle, Directors' Report Section 8). Shares are listed on both BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited. On capital deployment intent, the only stated policy is qualitative: BRSR Principle 2 reports that 100% of capital expenditure went into technologies improving environmental and social impacts in both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25, while the corresponding R&D line is a dash (stated nil). The material-subsidiary policy and the board-diversity policy are likewise published on the Company website. No capital-allocation philosophy statement, payout-ratio target or leverage policy is articulated anywhere in the routed text.
- NO ESG TARGET HAS ACTUALLY BEEN SET - the single most important ESG finding, and it is a stated absence, not silence. BRSR Section B Q5 ('Specific commitments, goals and targets set by the entity with defined timelines, if any') answers: 'The Company has carried out materiality assessment to arrive at their key material aspects relevant to their business. Future goals and targets on the key material aspects will be set and performance will be monitored.' Q6, performance against commitments/goals/targets, is a dash - a stated nil. There is therefore no emissions, energy, water, waste or diversity target with a date anywhere in this report. (Back-filled with provenance from the sibling profile.txt bundle, BRSR Section B; the risks_esg routing carries Section A and the material-issues table only.)
- Policy coverage gap on human rights, and an unexplained one: BRSR Section B Q1(a) answers 'No' for Principle 5 (human rights) - the entity's policies do NOT cover that principle - and Q3 confirms the policies do not extend to value-chain partners for P5. Q1(b) shows board approval only for Principles 1 to 4; Principles 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 policies are NOT board approved. DEFECT: Q12, which must give reasons where not all principles are covered, is answered 'Not applicable' on every line, contradicting the 'No' recorded at Q1(a). (Provenance: sibling profile.txt bundle, BRSR Section B.)
- No independent evaluation of the ESG policy framework: BRSR Section B Q11 states 'The company has not carried out assessment/ evaluation by external agency.' Board oversight of sustainability is delegated to a single executive - the Board 'has delegated the authority to Whole-Time Director who is responsible for decision-making on sustainability related issues', with Mr. Mehul Vala (WTD & CEO, DIN 08361696) named as the highest authority for the Business Responsibility policies. There is no board sustainability/ESG committee. (Provenance: sibling profile.txt bundle, BRSR Section B Q8, Q9, Q11.)
- Assurance is real but narrow: the BRSR carries Limited Assurance from MITCON Consultancy & Engineering Services Limited - a genuine external check that many mid-cap peers skip - but the reporting boundary is standalone only ('Disclosures made in this report are on a standalone basis'), and all three wholly owned subsidiaries (Responsive Industries Limited Hong Kong, Responsive Industries LLC USA, Axiom Cordages Limited Hong Kong) are recorded as NOT participating in the listed entity's Business Responsibility initiatives. Since the consolidated business is materially larger than the standalone entity, most of the group sits outside every ESG number in this report.
- Sustainable sourcing does not exist as a process: BRSR Principle 2 Q2(a) 'Does the entity have procedures in place for sustainable sourcing?' is answered 'No', with the follow-up percentage marked 'NA'. For a company whose core input is imported PVC resin, the absence of any sourcing procedure is material. (Provenance: sibling capex_expansion.txt bundle, BRSR Principle 2.)
- Circularity claim, unquantified: 'The Company has optimized its processes to the point where the majority of the waste produced is recycled and reused in its own operations. As a result, the amount of waste that is discharged from the Company is very minimal.' No tonnage, percentage or category split is given, and the Extended Producer Responsibility question that follows is cut off mid-word in the routed text, so EPR applicability for a plastics manufacturer cannot be read. (Provenance: sibling capex_expansion.txt bundle, BRSR Principle 2 Q3/Q4.)
- 100% of capital expenditure in both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25 is reported as directed to specific technologies improving the environmental and social impacts of products and processes, while the parallel R&D row is a dash - a stated nil, i.e. no R&D investment in such technologies in either year. The 'Details of improvements' column is left blank, so the claim is unverifiable from the report. (Provenance: sibling capex_expansion.txt bundle, BRSR Principle 2 Essential Indicator 1.)
- Certified management systems at the manufacturing unit: ISO 9001:2015 (quality), ISO 14001:2015 (environment), OHSMS/ISO 45001:2018 (occupational health & safety) and Bureau of Indian Standards. The unit has designated safety personnel, safety committees and regular safety training, and collaborates with external partners to embed health and safety in production processes.
- Occupational health and safety practice: free annual health check-ups for both permanent and contractual workers at the factory, a tie-up with a hospital in the vicinity of the factory for direct casualty transfer in emergencies, and factory-level provision of ventilation, hygiene and sanitation, safety audits, emergency exits and first aid. No lost-time-injury, fatality or near-miss statistics appear in the routed text.
- Diversity profile is weak and concentrated at the bottom: 275 permanent employees comprise 238 male (86.55%) and 37 female (13.45%); all 102 permanent workers are male (100%, with the female column a dash); the Board has 1 woman of 6 (16.67%); and Key Management Personnel are 4 with 0 women (0%). Differently abled employees and workers are 0 across every category, permanent and other-than-permanent, male and female. 'Other than Permanent' employees and workers are shown as dashes throughout - a stated nil contract workforce, which for a 100-acre manufacturing campus is itself notable.
- Employee turnover is rising: permanent-employee turnover of 9.02% in FY 2025-26 against 8.15% in FY 2024-25 and 2.16% in FY 2023-24. DEFECT: the table asks for a male/female/total split for each of the three years but only a single figure per year is printed, so which measure is being reported cannot be determined, and the entire 'Permanent Workers' row is blank rather than dashed - unknown, not nil.
- Zero-complaint and zero-penalty record across the board, disclosed as explicit nils rather than omissions: no complaints filed or pending in FY26 or FY25 from any of the six stakeholder groups (Communities, Investors other than shareholders, Shareholders, Employees & Workers, Customers, Value Chain Partners), each with a grievance mechanism and a published web link; nil monetary and non-monetary fines, penalties, settlements and compounding fees, with the statement 'During the year, no fines and penalties (monetary or non-monetary) was reported against any Directors and KMPs of the Company'; nil disciplinary actions for bribery/corruption against Directors, KMPs, employees or workers in either year; and nil conflict-of-interest complaints in either year. An Anti-Corruption Compliance Policy exists within the Whistle-Blower Policy and Code of Conduct. (Provenance: partly sibling profile.txt / capex_expansion.txt bundles, BRSR Principle 1.)
- Training and awareness coverage reported at 100% of every category - Board of Directors (3 programmes: operations scale, regulatory changes, directors' rights and responsibilities), KMPs (2 programmes) and other employees (2 programmes) on Code of Conduct, POSH, work ethics, whistle blower, insider trading, compliance, customer service and data privacy, and Workers (1 programme) on safety protocols, fire fighting and on-the-job training. (Provenance: sibling profile.txt bundle, BRSR Principle 1 Essential Indicator 1.)
- The ESG narrative statement by the responsible director is entirely qualitative - commitment to 'advancing sustainability across every aspect of its value chain', 'transparent reporting, stakeholder engagement, and continuous improvement' and confidence that the 'ESG-led approach will not only enhance stakeholder trust but also position us for sustainable and inclusive growth' - with no metric, baseline or date attached to any of it. NGRBC review is stated to occur internally by the Board/Committee annually, with statutory compliance reported to the Board quarterly. (Provenance: sibling profile.txt bundle, BRSR Section B Q7 and Q10.)
- MATERIAL-ISSUES TABLE DEFECTS worth carrying downstream: only three material responsible-business-conduct issues are disclosed (Business Ethics & Culture, Product Safety and Quality, Data Privacy and Cyber Security) and the table is cut off after the third row, so the roster may be incomplete; the 'financial implications' column is qualitative in every row with no quantification anywhere; Product Safety and Quality is classified as an 'Opportunity' even though its own rationale and implications describe recall, litigation and reputational RISK; and the same row's mitigation text refers to 'cleaner and safer mobility', automotive boilerplate that does not belong in a PVC flooring and synthetic-leather company's BRSR and points to a copied template. Notably, NO climate, emissions, energy or water issue appears among the material issues of a plastics manufacturer.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: NO capex or expansion project is disclosed anywhere in this bundle - this is a stated-absence finding, not a gap in routing. The Company operates a single 'state-of-the-art manufacturing factory and infrastructure set-up' at Boisar, Palghar district, Thane, Maharashtra, described in the Corporate Overview as a '100-acre integrated manufacturing campus', which currently caters to the domestic market along with the Middle East, Europe and North America. The BRSR Section A location table records National: 1 plant and 2 offices, and International: 1 plant and 2 offices - the international plant is never named, located or described anywhere in the routed text, which is a notable disclosure gap for a company that reports a foreign manufacturing site. The only forward capacity statement management makes is in the one-sentence MD&A Outlook: 'With Company's increased capacity utilization, strong product development, market efforts, the Company is optimistic about its growth in the coming years' - i.e. growth is to come from filling existing capacity, not from adding it. No commissioning, debottlenecking, ramp-up, greenfield, brownfield, land acquisition, new line, new R&D centre or acquisition is mentioned. The only 'expansion' evidence of any kind is product-range expansion: two lines flagged 'Newly Launched' in the Corporate Overview - 'Wallcore' premium SPC wall panels (an adjacency from flooring into wall coverings) and 'Luxcore' hybrid flooring. Management separately notes as an industry dynamic that 'Backward integration is becoming a key competitive advantage' and that India remains heavily dependent on imported PVC resin, but states NO intention or project to backward integrate itself. On capex quality rather than quantum, BRSR Principle 2 Essential Indicator 1 states that 100% of capex investments were in specific technologies to improve the environmental and social impacts of products and processes, in both the current and previous financial year, while the corresponding R&D row is a dash - a stated nil, i.e. no R&D investment in such technologies in either year (the 'Details of improvements' column is left blank). PROVENANCE/DEFECT NOTES: (1) The '=== NAMED DISCLOSURE - CAPITAL COMMITMENTS ===' block [page 146] carries NO figure at all - it reproduces only the opening of accounting policy note 2.20 'Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Capital Commitments' and is cut off mid-sentence at '...will be required to settle the obligation and a'. There is therefore no readable capital-commitment amount, date or unit, so capex_disclosed is correctly empty rather than guessed. (2) WRONG CHAPTER UNDER HEADING: the '=== CHAIRMAN / MD MESSAGE ===' section contains no chairman's or MD's message at all - it delivers BRSR Section C Principle 1 (fines/penalties, anti-bribery, conflict of interest, accounts-payable days, concentration of purchases/sales) and the start of Principle 2. The '=== BOARD'S / DIRECTORS' REPORT ===' section routed into this capex bundle contains subsidiary listing and board/KMP appointment-cessation content (Sections 10-19), nothing capex-related. (3) TRUNCATION at both ends: the MD&A extract is cut mid-sentence in Section 7 ('The committee makes n'); the Directors' Report extract begins mid-word ('ny Secretaries conducted a Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit') and ends mid-heading ('...MANAGERIAL PERSONNEL) R'); the Corporate Overview extract ends mid-contents-list ('Annexure A'); the BRSR extract ends mid-word ('...applicable to the en').
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The Indian market for PVC-based products is described as being in a strong expansion phase, driven by construction, infrastructure, urban housing, commercial interiors, automotive, logistics and export manufacturing; the overall market outlook for 2025-2030 is called 'structurally positive'.
- Named demand drivers: urbanization and affordable housing; commercial real estate and hospitality growth; warehousing/logistics parks; metro rail, airports and healthcare infrastructure; a shift toward low-maintenance materials; and increasing domestic manufacturing under 'Make in India'.
- Product-attribute drivers: durability, low maintenance cost, easy installation, wide range of designs and colours, affordability and resistance to moisture are cited as likely to drive the India vinyl flooring market over the forecast period.
- Industry estimate cited by management (attributed to Vinyl India 2025, not to the Company): Indian PVC demand could reach ~7 million tonnes by FY2030 at a ~7-8% CAGR.
- Lifestyle-led demand: rising interest in minimalist and modern interior design, design customisation flexibility, exposure to global design inspiration, and growing DIY home-improvement preference on the back of ease of installation.
- Adoption in commercial spaces such as offices, hospitals and schools on resilience and longevity grounds, plus rising infrastructure and real-estate investment, are named as impetus for market growth.
- Margin headwind explicitly flagged: margin pressure from imported PVC resin and Chinese competition 'remains a major concern'; India remains heavily dependent on imported PVC resin and Chinese oversupply is suppressing prices globally.
- Cost/regulatory brakes: volatility in resin prices may hinder industry expansion in coming years, stringent VOC-emission regulation and changing environmental policies could affect business prospects, and high installation cost is named as the primary restraint on market growth.
- External-shock commentary attached to the deterioration in working-capital and coverage metrics: 'Surged tariffs and escalating war tension impacted the business of the Company' and 'Geopolitical tensions and war increased global instability and economic stress' (the associated ratio figures sit in the MD&A key-ratio table and are deliberately not reproduced here).
- Management's own outlook sentence is short and unquantified: 'With Company's increased capacity utilization, strong product development, market efforts, the Company is optimistic about its growth in the coming years.' No revenue, margin or volume guidance is given anywhere in this bundle.

deepdive.thesis: Responsive Industries has transformed from a low-margin exporter to a high-margin, brand-driven resilient flooring leader by capturing premium demand in the U.S. B2C market and institutional sectors in India, leveraging China+1 supply chain shifts and product innovation. With zero debt, high EBITDA margins (24%), and a clear path to INR 2,500cr revenue by FY27 without new CapEx, the company is positioned for sustained profitability.

risks.note: Management states 'margin pressure from imported PVC resin and Chinese competition remains a major concern' even while calling the 2025-2030 market outlook structurally positive, and lists as important industry dynamics that 'India remains heavily dependent on imported PVC resin', 'Chinese oversupply is suppressing prices globally' and 'Domestic players are lobbying for anti-dumping and BIS protections'. It separately warns that 'Volatility in raw material prices due to fluctuation in resin prices may hinder industry expansion over coming years'. This is the sharpest structural risk in the report because the Company is a single-input, single-polymer manufacturer with no disclosed backward integration - management itself notes 'Backward integration is becoming a key competitive advantage' without claiming to have any, so the relief valve it identifies is one it does not hold. Any protection would come from anti-dumping/BIS action the Company does not control.
risks.risk: Imported PVC resin dependence and Chinese oversupply - a structural squeeze on the Company's only input and its selling prices

risks.note: The MD&A states 'The Company is engaged only in single segment of products i.e. PVC products'; BRSR Section A item 16 shows one main activity, Manufacturing, at 100% of turnover; and BRSR item 18 records just one national plant (plus two offices), the Boisar facility in Palghar district, Thane, Maharashtra. Every rupee of standalone revenue therefore depends on one polymer, one process family and one physical site - fire, flood, labour action, a Maharashtra pollution-control order or a resin-supply interruption at Boisar has no fallback. A second, international plant appears in the BRSR location table but is never named, located or described anywhere in the report, so it cannot be relied on as redundancy.
risks.risk: Single-segment, single-domestic-plant concentration - no diversification anywhere in the operating structure

risks.note: BRSR item 19(b) puts exports at 30.45% of total turnover, with more than 300 international distributors across 70 countries and an extensive retail presence in Europe and North America - i.e. roughly a third of standalone revenue sits outside India's jurisdiction and currency. Management links this directly to FY26 damage, commenting in the key-ratio disclosure that 'Surged tariffs and escalating war tension impacted the business of the Company' and that 'Geopolitical tensions and war increased global instability and economic stress' (the associated ratio figures are deliberately not reproduced here). This is a stated, realised risk rather than a hypothetical one, and the Company has no disclosed hedging, alternative-market or tariff-mitigation plan.
risks.risk: Export concentration colliding with tariffs and war - management explicitly attributes damage to it this year

risks.note: Management's own commentary on its key financial ratios flags a material lengthening of debtor days, explained by surged tariffs and escalating war tension, and a decline in interest coverage explained by geopolitical tension and war; it also notes the current ratio rose because of an increase in trade receivables coupled with a decrease in short-term borrowings. Read qualitatively, cash is being absorbed into receivables rather than released, and the improvement in one headline liquidity ratio is partly an artefact of that absorption - a durable watch-item for anyone tracking this company. Numeric ratio values are deliberately not reproduced here.
risks.risk: Receivables and working-capital stretch tied to the export channel

risks.note: The MD&A states that as on March 31, 2026 the Company had 273 employees against 358 in the previous year - a reduction of roughly a quarter of the payroll in a single year - while asserting industrial relations at the factory 'have remained cordial' and offering no explanation for the decline. The BRSR reports 275 permanent employees and 102 permanent workers at the same date, which does not reconcile with the MD&A's 273 figure, and reports permanent-employee turnover of 9.02% in FY26 against 8.15% and 2.16% in the two prior years (a rising trend), with the permanent-workers turnover row left entirely blank. For a business whose only manufacturing know-how sits at one site, a shrinking and increasingly mobile workforce with contradictory reporting is a structural, not cosmetic, concern.
risks.risk: Sharp workforce contraction and inconsistent headcount disclosure

risks.note: The BRSR material-issues table identifies Product Safety and Quality (classified, oddly, as an Opportunity) and states that 'any loose end in the product maintenance or quality may pose it to material risks', with financial implications spelled out as product recalls, damaged consumer quality perception, reputational harm and increased costs from replacements, field service, product fixes and litigation. The MD&A reinforces the regulatory leg: 'stringent regulations related to volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emissions coupled with changing environmental policies could also affect overall business prospects during forecasted timeframe'. PVC flooring sold into healthcare, education and transportation is exactly the category where VOC and indoor-air-quality rules tighten first, and roughly a third of output goes to jurisdictions (Europe, North America) that regulate this most aggressively. NOTE A CLEAR TEMPLATE DEFECT IN THIS ROW: the mitigation text reads 'Our product responsibility extends beyond manufacturing and sales, contributing to cleaner and safer mobility' - 'mobility' is automotive-sector boilerplate that does not describe a PVC flooring and synthetic-leather business, indicating this material-issue row was copied from another company's BRSR.
risks.risk: Product safety, quality and VOC/environmental regulation of PVC products

risks.note: Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a Risk with negative financial implications: 'technology failures or cyberattacks can disrupt operations, leading to downtime and loss of productivity'. Stated mitigations are firewalls, encryption, multi-factor authentication, regular security audits, employee education and adoption of global data protection standards, plus regular assessment for system vulnerabilities, compliance gaps and technological obsolescence. No incidents, breaches or spend are disclosed, and there is no board-level technology committee.

The first material issue in the BRSR table, classified as a Risk: 'Non-compliance of code of conduct and business ethics affects the work environment and profitability of the Company and may also cause financial or reputational impact', with negative financial implications from disruption and reputational damage. The only stated mitigation is regular employee training on the Code of Conduct. This risk sits alongside a related-party disclosure whose AOC-2 paragraph is self-contradictory (it simultaneously suggests material related-party transactions may exist and that no information need be provided) and a BRSR that reports the entire related-party-share block as dashes.
